questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

In 2015, a large mining company said it would reduce the number of staff by 6000 and sell its less profitable mines in an attempt to become more efficient. If it is successful, what is most likely to happen to its costs? total variable total fixed cost average cost cost

options.A: fall fall fall
options.C: fall no change fall

questions.questionText: The production of a firm which operates in an imperfectly competitive market gives rise to external production costs. Which statement about this firm must be correct?

options.A: External costs exceed external benefits.
options.C: Social costs exceed private costs.

The diagram shows the cost curves for a firm. MC price ATC AFC O Q Q

options.A: different different
options.C: same different

options.A: B TR revenue revenue TR O O output output
options.C: D TR revenue revenue TR O O output output

questions.questionText: Many public utilities can be described as ‘natural’ monopolies. Which statement best describes the situation leading to a ‘natural’ monopoly?

options.A: There are high fixed costs and falling average costs over all outputs demanded.
options.B: There are legal restrictions on new entrants.
options.C: A single firm controls the supply of raw materials.
options.D: The firm has a patent on an essential process.

questions.questionText: Increased advertising by a firm in an imperfectly competitive industry leads to an increase in demand for the industry’s product but a fall in the firm’s profits. What could help to explain this?

options.A: Production is subject to diseconomies of scale.
options.B: Rival firms respond by increasing their advertising outlays.
options.C: The demand for the industry’s product is price-inelastic.
options.D: The increase in demand for the firm’s output is entirely at the expense of other firms.

questions.questionText: An industry consists of a dominant firm, which acts as a price leader, and a large number of small firms. Which statement about the profit-maximising output of the small firms is correct?

options.A: Average cost is equal to average revenue.
options.C: Marginal cost is equal to price.

questions.questionText: There are two firms in an industry. Firm X faces a choice. It can either act independently or work with its rival. If it acts independently its profit could be $900 a week but it could be only $400 a week depending on what its rival does. If it works with its rival the joint profit of the two firms together would be $1400, $700 each. It has no knowledge of what the rival’s policy will be. Which concept describes this situation?

options.A: contestable market
options.C: principal agent problem

questions.questionText: What explains the kinked demand curve model of price rigidity in oligopoly?

options.A: collusion between all firms in the industry in the setting of prices
options.B: the assumption that a single firm acts as price leader for all firms in the industry
options.C: the individual firm’s expectations about other firms’ responses to its price changes
options.D: the presence of barriers to the entry of new firms into the industry

questions.questionText: Which policy is not designed to correct a market failure?

options.A: government provision of health care
options.C: price controls on large firms

questions.questionText: A tax system allows people to earn a certain sum of income free of income tax. On income above this level, tax is levied at a constant rate. Which diagram correctly shows how marginal and average rates of tax vary with income?

options.A: B rate rate marginal of tax of tax marginal average average O O income income
options.C: D rate rate of tax of tax marginal average = marginal average O O income income

questions.questionText: What is the best example of nudge theory as applied to the prevention of tax evasion?

options.A: employing an extensive administration to ensure detection of evasion
options.B: imposing heavy penalties to deter offending behaviour
options.C: providing information to taxpayers about the undesirable effects of tax evasion
options.D: requiring employers to inform the tax authorities of workers’ pay

questions.questionText: In many countries it has been observed that, when high marginal rates of income tax imposed on richer groups are reduced, the tax revenue raised increases. What is an implication of this observation?

options.A: Government policy should aim to minimise the income tax.
options.B: Sales taxes are always superior to income taxes as a means of raising revenue for the government.
options.C: Tax policy intended to reduce income tax on the rich may make the poor better off.
options.D: The government should always levy proportional rather than progressive income taxes.

How might real GNP per head be adjusted to make it a more reliable indicator when comparing standards of living in different countries?

options.A: adjustments to allow for differences in population size in different countries
options.B: adjustments to allow for differences in rates of inflation in different countries
options.C: adjustments to allow for differences in the relative size of the hidden economy in different countries
options.D: the use of market exchange rates rather than purchasing power parity exchange rates

questions.questionText: Which combination of circumstances is most likely to lead to an increase in a country’s budget deficit? discretionary total GDP unemployment government spending

options.A: decreases rises decreases
options.C: increases falls increases

questions.questionText: To combat a rising crime rate, the government decides to recruit additional police officers who are paid a wage equal to that which they previously earned in the private sector. As long as their previous jobs remain unfilled, what effect will the recruitment of the additional police officers have on the national income and on economic welfare? effect on effect on national income economic welfare

options.A: increase unchanged
options.C: unchanged decrease

questions.questionText: What could not exist in a closed, mixed economy?

options.A: a balance of trade deficit
options.C: household debt

questions.questionText: What does the accelerator principle state?

options.A: Consumption is a function of the rate of change of income.
options.B: Income is a function of the rate of change of investment.
options.C: Investment is a function of the rate of change of income.
options.D: Investment is a function of the rate of interest.

questions.questionText: What would not be classified as structural unemployment?

options.A: a car worker who is replaced by a robot on the production line
options.B: a coal miner whose mine closes because of increased use of solar power
options.C: a fruit picker who cannot find work in the winter months
options.D: a textile worker whose factory closes as production moves abroad

questions.questionText: What represents a leakage from the circular flow of income in an economy?

options.A: a balance of trade surplus
options.C: reduction in funds for research and development

questions.questionText: What will cause a downward shift in the aggregate demand curve of an economy?

options.A: an increase in firms’ stocks of raw materials
options.B: a decrease in the export of goods
options.C: a decrease in the propensity to import

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to raise the level of total demand in an economy?

options.A: an increase in direct taxation matched by a reduction in indirect taxation
options.C: cuts in public expenditure matched by tax cuts

questions.questionText: The government cuts taxes and increases its spending in order to create jobs during a recession. When will a resulting budget deficit be least likely to cause a permanent reduction in unemployment?

options.A: when households expect higher inflation rates in the future
options.B: when households spend their extra disposable incomes on domestic products
options.C: when the government’s extra spending is on new infra-structure projects
options.D: when the government’s extra spending is on the salaries of public sector workers

questions.questionText: In 2011, the global money supply, narrowly defined, rose 11% and broadly defined money increased roughly 8%, as central banks continued efforts to keep interest rates low. What type of policy does this statement illustrate?

options.A: contractionary fiscal
options.C: expansionary fiscal

questions.questionText: Which policy measure would be most likely to reduce a developing economy’s birth rate and its household saving ratio?

options.A: an increase in student tuition fees
options.C: the introduction of a basic state pension
